newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh further delays trial for Mujib killing.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh further delays trial for Mujib killing.

text.p: The trial of six accused in the 1975 killing of Bangladesh independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was further delayed on Monday when defence attorneys sought copies of case documents from the prosecution.
Judge Kazi Golam Rasul said the hearing would resume on April 6.

The six accused in the August 1975 killing of Mujib, father of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, in the country's first army coup appeared briefly before a makeshift court adjoining the central jail in the capital of Dhaka. Security was tight.
Court officials said 14 others accused in the case have either left the country or were hiding in Bangladesh. Most of the accused are retired army officers.
Public prosecutors were to file formal charges against the accused on Monday, but the move was delayed after the defence called for copies of prosecution reports on the charges, officials said.
The trial looked deadlocked at this stage as attorneys on both sides argued over pre-hearing formalities.
Defence lawyers demanded "better treatment by jail authorities of the accused, who have been confined to solitary cells."
"This is a clear violation of human rights," said defence attorney Mahbubur Rahman.

The trial was delayed for more than two decades because Mujib's successors had protected the 1975 coup leaders from law under a special ordinance. Bangladesh's parliament annulled the ordinance after Hasina took office last June.
